notes.text: Open — O ye porters, appointed by God for this work. The gates - Of the Lord's tabernacle: where the rule of righteousness was kept and taught, and the sacrifices of righteousness were offered.

The righteous — As David was a type of Christ and the temple of heaven, so this place hath a farther prospect than David, and relates to Christ's ascending into heaven, and opening the gates of that blessed temple, both for himself and for all believers.

The builders — The commonwealth of Israel and the church of God are here and elsewhere compared to a building, wherein, as the people are the stones, so the princes and rulers are the builders. And as these master-builders rejected David, so their successors rejected Christ. Head stone - The chief stone in the whole building, by which the several parts of the building are upheld and firmly united together. Thus David united all the tribes and families of Israel: and thus Christ united Jews and Gentiles together. And therefore this place is justly expounded of Christ, Mark xii, 10 Acts iv, 11 Rom. ix, 32 Eph. ii, 20. And to him the words agree more properly than to David.
Made — Or sanctified as a season never to be forgotten.
We — These seem to be the words of the Levites, to whom he spake ver. 19.

Blessed — We pray that God would bless his person and government. Cometh - To the throne; or from his Father into the world: who is known by the name of him that cometh or was to come, and of whom this very word is used, Gen. xlix, 10 Isaiah xxxv, 4. Name - By commission from him. We - We who are the Lord's ministers attending upon him in his house, and appointed to bless in his name, Num. vi, 23 Deut. x, 8. So these are the words of the priests.

The Lord — Or, The mighty God, as this name of God signifies, and as he shewed himself to be by this, his wonderful work. Who - Who hath scattered our dark clouds, and put us into a state of peace, and safety, and happiness. The horns - These are supposed to be made for this very use, that the beasts should be bound and killed there. These three last verses are David's words. Because this psalm was very large, and the matter of it of the greatest importance, the psalmist thought fit to divide it into two and twenty several parts, according to the number of the Hebrew letters, that he might both prevent tediousness, and fix it in the memory. Each part consists of eight verses. All the verses of the first part beginning with Aleph, all the verses of the second with Beth, and so on. It is observable, that the word of God is here called by the names of law, statutes, precepts or commandments, judgments, ordinances, righteousness, testimonies, way and word. By which variety, he designed to express the nature and perfection of God's word. It is called his word, as revealed by him to us; his way, as prescribed by him for us to walk in; his law, as binding us to obedience; his statutes, as declaring his authority of giving us laws; his precepts as directing our duty; his ordinances, as ordained by him; his righteousness, as exactly agreeable to God's righteous nature and will; his judgments, as proceeding from the great judge of the world, and being his judicial sentence to which all men must submit; and his testimonies, as it contains the witness of God's will, and of man's duty. And there is but one of these one hundred and seventy six verses, in which one or other of these titles is not found. The general scope and design of this psalm is, to magnify the law and make it honourable: to shew the excellency and usefulness of divine Revelation, and recommend it to us, by the psalmist's own example, who speaks by experience of the benefits of it, for which he praises God, and earnestly prays for the continuance of God's grace, to direct and quicken him in his way.

glossa.text:
*Let him now say.* ((ID.)) As I admonish you, so do you admonish one another; or, *let him say,* that is, let him confess.

*Because for ever.* Behold four verses of one ending.

*Open ye.* ((CASS.)) In the third place he desires that the gates of Jerusalem be opened to him, where he speaks also of the corner stone. Open, O prophets, who bear the keys of the kingdom of heaven. *The gates.* ((CASS., HIER.)) They who have entered through these gates of doctrine praise truly; outside the Catholic Church there is no praise of God. ((CASS.)) All these gates lead to one, which is Christ, through whom the just enter into heaven; whence: *I am the door, through which if any man enter in, he shall be safe ((Joan. X))* . And elsewhere: *No man cometh to the Father, but by me ((Joan. XIV))*. ((AUG.)) Behold, he has made mention of both worlds: and because this gate has appeared as Christ, *I will confess to thee,* giving thanks with gladness, *because thou hast heard* at the coming of the Son; for the just of former times were asking for the coming. *The gates of justice.* That is, the gates of death, etc., *as far as* that is, through it unto life.
*They that build.* ((ID.)) The Jews alone, worshipping God, were building, the rest being destroyed through idolatry; but they did not finish, because they despised Christ.
*This is done by the Lord.* Or, *This is done by the Lord for him,* according to another reading. ((ID.)) That is, unto the honour of the Father.

*This is the day.* This is the jubilee year, figuratively observed under the law, which is called *remitting,* or *beginning,* because then bondmen were set free, possessions were restored to their owners: and we on this day have been redeemed from the servitude of sin, to whom an eternal inheritance has been restored. ((CASS.)) *This is the day.* Although he made all days, this one singularly, on which the Lord came, on which it is fitting to rejoice, because the devil lost his right and man lived again; and because this is so,
*O Lord, save,* etc. Behold the desire of a great petition. *Save,* from the ruin of the world. *Give prosperity,* that these sorrows may be turned into eternal joys.

*Blessed,* etc. ((CASS.)) Fourthly he urges that the courts of God be frequented, rejoicing in the coming of Christ. ((AUG.)) Cursed therefore is he that comes in his own name, etc., *as far as* he who shall be cursed. ((CASS.)) *Blessed.* Praise for the coming; and, O ye other Christians, we the elders, as it were priests, *have blessed you,* which profits much, because *we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.*

*Out of the house.* ((ID.)) That is, the Catholic Church, etc., *as far as* because glad is the confession that follows benefits.

*Appoint a day.* ((AUG.)) The great, who go beyond, who with the mind touch the Word, God with God, etc., *as far as* that is, that he may attain unto eternal joys.

 *A solemn day.* In the old law ((Deut. X.)) the Pasch, Pentecost, the feast of tabernacles, three chief solemnities, in which it was commanded that no man should appear empty in the sight of the Lord. He is empty who has not Christ in himself, who is the foundation, which no man is able to change. Hence it is that on those three solemnities the faithful people offers a coin by an offering of the hand, signifying the inward offering. For on a coin there is the name and image of the king. Let each one therefore offer a coin spiritually, that he may have in himself the *name* of the king, that is, of Christ, being called a Christian from Christ; and may show forth to God the *image,* that is, the soul, marked with the light of his countenance. *The horn of the altar.* ((CASS.)) Or by the *altar* is understood the sacrament of the body and blood, etc., *as far as he shall not have life everlasting.*

Or, the *altar* is understood to be the mind of man; whence in the law it was commanded ((Exod. XXVII)) that an altar be made four-cornered and hollow: four-cornered, because the human mind ought to be fortified with four virtues, prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance; and the same ought to be hollow to receive the word of God and the fire of love. For swelling drives back what is poured in; whence in Leviticus it is commanded ((Levit. I)) that the little bladder of the throat and the feathers be cast away, when a turtle-dove or a pigeon is offered. The bladder signifies the puffing up of pride; the feathers, empty searchings into lofty things; cast these away therefore, that thou mayest be a hollow altar.

*Thou art my God.* And that we may speak more openly, this is the sense of these words: Let not this feast day upon earth, on which the lamb was slain, suffice: but let it be appointed in frequent celebrations, until with minds exalted we come to his inward Godhead, where we shall sing praises thus: *Thou art my God,* etc. And so, as he began with praise, so he ends with it.
*Give praise to the Lord.* From the beginning which we forsook, unto the end to which we return, there is nothing more wholesome, which may delight, than the praise of God

notes.text: Mark xi, 1; Luke xix, 29; John xii, 12.

The daughter of Sion — That is, the inhabitants of Jerusalem: the first words of the passage are cited from Isaiah lxii, 11; the rest from Zech. ix, 9. The ancient Jewish doctors were wont to apply these prophecies to the Messiah. On an ass - The Prince of Peace did not take a horse, a warlike animal. But he will ride on that by and by, Rev. xix, 11. In the patriarchal ages, illustrious persons thought it no disgrace to make use of this animal: but it by no means appears, that this opinion prevailed, or this custom continued, till the reign of Tiberias. Was it a mean attitude wherein our Lord then appeared? Mean even to contempt! I grant it: I glory in it: it is for the comfort of my soul for the honour of his humility, and for the utter confusion of all worldly pomp and grandeur.
They set him thereon — That is, on the clothes.
A great multitude spread their garments in the way — A custom which was usual at the creation of a king, 2 Kings ix, 13.

The multitudes cried, saying — Probably from a Divine impulse; for certainly most of them understood not the words they uttered. Hoseanna - (Lord save us) was a solemn word in frequent use among the Jews. The meaning is, "We sing hosanna to the Son of David. Blessed is he, the Messiah, of the Lord. Save. Thou that art in the highest heavens." Our Lord restrained all public tokens of honour from the people till now, lest the envy of his enemies should interrupt his preaching before the time. But this reason now ceasing, he suffered their acclamations, that they might be a public testimony against their wickedness, who in four or five days after cried out, Crucify him, crucify him. The expressions recorded by the other evangelists are somewhat different from these: but all of them were undoubtedly used by some or others of the multitude.

This is Jesus from Nazareth — What a stumbling block was this! if he was of Nazareth, he could not be the Messiah. But they who earnestly desired to know the truth would not stumble thereat: for upon inquiry (which such would not fail to make) they would find, he was not of Nazareth, but Bethlehem.

glossa.text: *And when they drew nigh.* Here Matthew passes over the things that were done before he entered Jerusalem, which the others treat at greater length. *And when they drew nigh.* The Lord drew nigh to Jerusalem spiritually when he was made flesh, he visited the Church, in which is the vision of peace, and reconciled her to himself by confession. For Bethphage is called the house of the mouth. *Bethphage.* Bethphage was a hamlet of priests on mount Olivet, on the side of which mountain is the town of Bethany. Bethphage, the house of the mouth. Bethany, the house of obedience. These the Lord, journeying to Jerusalem, exalts by his presence, because before his passion he filled many by his teaching with the gifts of devout confession and of obedience. And those towns are set on the mount of Olives, that is, in Christ the Lord, from whom anointing and light come to all; whence: *A city cannot be hid, set upon a mountain.--To mount Olivet: then Jesus,* etc. Looking to the loftiness of mercy, ἔλεος is interpreted *mercy.* The nature of oil is to be the servant of light, and the solace of labours and of pains, and it excels the other liquids. *He sent.* Because he does not wish the lamp which he received to be hidden under a bushel. *Two disciples.* Two, as being about to preach the knowledge of truth and cleanness of work, and the sacrament of the twofold love. Some say that these two are Peter and Philip, who first brought Gentiles to Christ, Philip, Samaria, which they interpret as the *she-ass*, Peter, Cornelius, as it were the colt of Samaria.

*And the colt.* The colt is the people of the Gentiles, on which none of the teachers had put the bridle of correction, free and wanton, which itself also was ensnared in the bonds of sins. *For all have sinned and need the grace of God ((Rom. III))* . Others, of the colt only: Matthew, who writes to the Hebrews, speaks also of the she-ass, teaching that salvation is not to be despaired of for the Hebrews if they repent. Mark says that the colt was found before the gate where two ways met. The gate is Christ, outside which the people of the Gentiles stood bound: not in the one way of faith, but in divers errors.

*Tell ye the daughter of Sion.* The daughter of Sion is Jerusalem, set on mount Sion. Mystically. The Church belonging to the Jerusalem above, which is the mother of us all, of which no small part was then in the people of Israel. *King.* Lest you say: *We have no king but Caesar ((Joan. XIX))*. *To thee.* If thou believest; against thee if thou believest not. *Upon a she-ass,* etc. He did not sit upon both according to the letter, but in the hearts of both peoples. The Lord could go up upon both, coming down from the one, and going up upon the other.

*And they brought.* So the apostles also loosed the world by the power of Christ from the power of the devil, and laid their garments upon it. But the rest of the crowd, that is, the Jews, strew their garments, that is, the commandments of the law, because they were to be trodden underfoot by Christians, in the way, that is, in Christ. *Upon them.* The garments of the apostles are the divine precepts and spiritual grace, by which the foulness of our flesh is covered. Naked of these before, but now adorned by the apostles, the peoples have Christ for their rider. The lesser crowd does not put its garments upon the she-ass, but in the way, and not where he might stumble: because the holy martyrs, putting off the flesh, prepare a way for the simpler sort by the example of their own blood.
*Branches from the trees,* etc. They cut branches or leafy boughs, because they culled words and sentences, or examples, from the books of the Fathers.

*Osanna. ((HIER.))* Osi, that is, save, make safe. Anna is the interjection of one entreating, as though, save, I beseech. Osanna is wholly Hebrew, and it signifies that the coming of Christ is the salvation of the world: whence there follows: *Blessed. Osanna,* that is, save. *In the highest.* Because the coming of Christ is the salvation not of men only but of the whole world, joining earthly things to heavenly, *that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, of things on earth, and of things under the earth ((Phil. II))*. *In the highest.* Because it is the salvation of the angels also, whose number he fills up.

*When he had entered.* He entered the city of Jerusalem often, but not with these praises: he is not called king, which he had always fled, save only now when he goes up to suffer. And this was done for this reason, that he might the more stir up their envy against himself, because the time of the passion was now at hand.

echoes.text: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your King comes to you! He is righteous, and having salvation; lowly, and riding on a donkey, even on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
echoes.note: Matthew's formula citation (21:4-5) of the prophesied king who comes 'humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.' Matthew uniquely reads the Hebrew parallelism woodenly, producing two animals (donkey and colt), which shapes his narrative of two beasts (21:7).

echoes.text: Behold, Yahweh has proclaimed to the end of the earth, “Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your salvation comes. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.’”
echoes.note: The opening of the citation, 'Tell the daughter of Zion, behold...,' is drawn from Isaiah 62:11 ('Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, your salvation comes') rather than from Zechariah, whose own opening is 'Rejoice greatly.' Matthew blends Isaiah 62:11 with Zechariah 9:9 into a single quotation.

echoes.text: Save us now, we beg you, Yahweh! Yahweh, we beg you, send prosperity now. Blessed is he who comes in Yahweh’s name! We have blessed you out of Yahweh’s house.
echoes.note: The crowd's cry (21:9) quotes Psalm 118:25-26: 'Hosanna' transliterates the Hebrew 'hoshia-na' ('save now,' Ps 118:25), and 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD' is verbatim from Ps 118:26 (LXX), a Hallel pilgrimage acclamation.

echoes.text: Then they hurried, and took every man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew the trumpet, saying, “Jehu is king.”
echoes.note: Spreading garments on the road as an act of royal acclamation: at Jehu's anointing the men 'took every man his garment, and put it under him... and blew the trumpet, saying, Jehu is king.' The crowd's gesture (21:8) enacts an enthronement.

echoes.text: The king said to them, “Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon. Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel. Blow the trumpet, and say, ‘Long live king Solomon!’ Then you shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne; for he shall be king in my place. I have appointed him to be prince over Israel and over Judah.” Benaiah the […]
echoes.note: Solomon is mounted on the king's mule and led to be made king amid rejoicing; the royal son of David enters his city riding a humble mount to acclamation, the pattern Jesus' entry evokes.

echoes.text: When your days are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men; but my loving kindness shall not […]
echoes.note: The repeated acclamation 'son of David' (21:9) invokes the Davidic covenant promise of an everlasting throne to David's offspring, framing Jesus' entry as the coming of the promised Davidic king.

echoes.text: And he entered into it on the three and twentieth day of the second month, in the hundred and seventy and first year, with praise and palm branches, and with harps, and with cymbals, and with viols, and with hymns, and with songs: because a great enemy was destroyed out of Israel.
echoes.note: Simon's entry into the Jerusalem citadel 'with praise and palm branches' provides a Second Temple template for entering the holy city with branches and acclamation, paralleling the multitude cutting and spreading branches (21:8).

echoes.text: Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey’s colt to the choice vine; he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
echoes.note: Jacob's blessing on Judah, 'binding his foal to the vine and his donkey's colt to the choice vine,' was read messianically (donkey + colt motif) in Jewish tradition and may stand behind the donkey imagery alongside Zechariah 9:9.

echoes.text: Sing, daughter of Zion! Shout, Israel! Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem. Yahweh has taken away your judgments. He has thrown out your enemy. The King of Israel, Yahweh, is in your midst. You will not be afraid of evil any more.
echoes.note: 'Rejoice, daughter of Zion... the King of Israel, even the LORD, is in your midst': a 'daughter of Zion' oracle announcing the arrival of the divine king, thematically resonant with the entry.

echoes.text: Yahweh your God will raise up to you a prophet from your midst, of your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him.
echoes.note: The crowd's identification of Jesus as 'the prophet' (21:11) may echo the promise of a prophet like Moses whom the people must heed.

echoes.text: Wherefore bearing wands wreathed with leaves, and fair boughs, and palms also, they offered up hymns of thanksgiving to him that had prosperously brought to pass the cleansing of his own place.
echoes.note: At the temple's rededication the people carried 'branches and beautiful boughs and palms' with hymns, a Hanukkah-style festal procession resembling the branch-waving acclamation of Jesus.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Open to me the gates of righteousness.
This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous enter.
Look, your king comes, humble, riding on a donkey.
Hosanna to the Son of David!
They spread their cloaks and palms along the road.
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Come, let us worship; this is the day the Lord has made.
Hosanna in the highest! Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Hear the road fill with shouting, cloaks thrown down in the dust, branches cut green and waving, a whole city leaning out to see.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
And there at the center, no warhorse, no army, only a borrowed colt and a man riding gentle into the noise.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
This is the day the Lord has made; the gates of righteousness swing wide, the stone the builders refused is set as the head.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Wave your branches; lift your voices; the King is passing, and the road runs straight to the cross. Come, let us worship.
Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is the one who comes! Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Open the gates; the King is at the door.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
No warhorse, only a donkey; cloaks and palms in the road.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
This is the day the Lord has made.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Come, let us worship the King who rides toward the cross.
Hosanna in the highest! Amen.
